newsitem.title: UK: NWE diesel demand lifts premium, U.S. arb closed.
newsitem.headline: NWE diesel demand lifts premium, U.S. arb closed.

text.p: Stronger demand boosted low sulphur diesel cargo premiums and NYMEX losses closed the U.S. arb for Russians in lacklustre business on Monday, traders said.
Volumes were again overshadowed by the 10-day-old AIC-Cargill standoff over a record high November IPE delivery.
Benchmark IPE futures ended $3.75 down at $219, following Brent's fall on U.N. and Iraqi statements that the way was clear for implementation of oil-for-food.
In barges, refinery grade heating oil traded unchanged at Dec IPE +$2 but low sulphur diesel sold around $1.50 lower at Dec IPE +$11.50.
Trade was moribund, with the Nov IPE play involving over 600,000 tonnes still absorbing considerable barge capacity in the Rotterdam region.
In cargoes, French quality heating oil was steady at Dec IPE +$5/6 for late November but low sulphur diesel was around $2 firmer at Dec IPE +$18/20.
Traders attributed low sulphur diesel strength to the absorption of recent trans-Atlantic cargoes and the lions' share of European refinery production going to heating oil.
A U.S. arb that earned New York heating oil plus 40 basis points for a Russian closed on NYMEX losses caused by Iraq news.
